findings.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — should_sync` only excludes the single immediate `sync_source` integration; `sync_group_assignee_outbound` (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:123) fans out to every linked external issue with that one source, so a 2nd-order bounce (A->Sentry assign tagged source=A -> outbound to B (allowed, not skipped) -> B's webhook treats the API write as new inbound change, tags source=B -> outbound fan-out again includes A, and A is NOT skipped because source is now B) completes an A->Sentry->B->Sentry->A loop; there is no visited-set/chain tracking, only last-hop exclusion, so 2+ integrations with bidirectional sync enabled can ping-pong indefinitely or fan out across N integrations.

src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 — queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default, which Python evaluates exactly once when the class body executes (module import time), not `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`; every `AssignmentSource` built via `from_integration()` (the only production call site, mixins/issues.py and utils/sync.py) omits `queued` and therefore gets the identical frozen timestamp captured at process start, making the field useless for any staleness/ordering/replay-protection use and silently wrong for all instances; existing test (tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:36) only asserts `queued is not None`, so this never surfaces in CI.

src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:28 — to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict()`, which serializes the raw `datetime` object from the (effectively constant, see other finding) `queued` field; this dict is passed straight into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})` (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:141). If the Celery broker uses JSON task serialization (Sentry's common convention), a raw `datetime` is not JSON-serializable and enqueueing would raise, silently breaking every outbound sync that carries an assignment_source. The unit tests that exercise this path (tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py, e.g. test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration) use `with self.tasks():`, which runs the task in-process/eagerly and bypasses real broker (de)serialization, so this would not be caught by the existing suite.

src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py:130 — assignment_source` is only threaded through to the single outbound task enqueued at the moment of `assign`/`deassign` and is never persisted on the `GroupAssignee` row itself; if two integrations (or an integration and a manual UI change) race to reassign the same group, each call independently snapshots `user_id`/`assignment_source` and fires its own outbound fan-out (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:135). Celery does not guarantee execution order between these tasks (and `sync_assignee_outbound` has `max_retries=5, default_retry_delay=300`, so a transient failure can delay one hop by many minutes), so a stale earlier assignment's outbound task can execute after a newer one and silently overwrite a different, more-recently and legitimately set external assignee, because `should_sync` only suppresses the loop back to that task's own originating integration, not against whatever the current DB state's true source is.

src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411 — sync_status_outbound`'s new `assignment_source` parameter is dead: it has no callers anywhere in the codebase (unlike `sync_assignee_outbound`, there is no `sync_status_outbound` task/caller), and even if invoked, `should_sync("outbound_status", ...)` is never called with a source, so the cycle-prevention guard added to `should_sync` is only wired for assignee sync, not status sync, leaving inconsistent/incomplete abstraction across the two sync paths

src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 — queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition/import time, not per-instance, so every `AssignmentSource` created via `from_integration()` (the only production constructor path, used in src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:96-99 and :115-119) gets the same frozen "queued" timestamp for the life of the worker process, silently breaking any staleness/ordering check that relies on it.

src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:17 — queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default evaluated once at class-definition/import time, not per-instance, so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` (i.e. every real call via `from_integration`) shares one stale timestamp; `test_to_dict` in tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py only asserts `queued is not None`, so this bug is not caught.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — should_sync` only excludes the single immediate `sync_source` integration; `sync_group_assignee_outbound` (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:123) fans out to every linked external issue with that one source, so a 2nd-order bounce (A->Sentry assign tagged source=A -> outbound to B (allowed, not skipped) -> B's webhook treats the API write as new inbound change, tags source=B -> outbound fan-out again includes A, and A is NOT skipped because source is now B) completes an A->Sentry->B->Sentry->A loop; there is no visited-set/chain tracking, only last-hop exclusion, so 2+ integrations with bidirectional sync enabled can ping-pong indefinitely or fan out across N integrations.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds loop-prevention in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` by skipping only when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (i.e., last-hop exclusion). `sync_group_assignee_outbound` still fans out one `assignment_source` to *all* linked external issues, and nothing in the diff tracks a chain/visited set across multiple integrations. So the reviewer’s point—that multi-integration bidirectional sync could still bounce A→B→A because the source changes each hop—is grounded in the new logic/its limitation. However, whether this becomes an actual infinite loop depends on external webhook behavior and idempotency not shown in the diff, so it’s better treated as an important architectural/edge-case concern rather than a strictly verifiable defect from the patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py:130 — assignment_source` is only threaded through to the single outbound task enqueued at the moment of `assign`/`deassign` and is never persisted on the `GroupAssignee` row itself; if two integrations (or an integration and a manual UI change) race to reassign the same group, each call independently snapshots `user_id`/`assignment_source` and fires its own outbound fan-out (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:135). Celery does not guarantee execution order between these tasks (and `sync_assignee_outbound` has `max_retries=5, default_retry_delay=300`, so a transient failure can delay one hop by many minutes), so a stale earlier assignment's outbound task can execute after a newer one and silently overwrite a different, more-recently and legitimately set external assignee, because `should_sync` only suppresses the loop back to that task's own originating integration, not against whatever the current DB state's true source is.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `assignment_source` is only passed through the call chain (`GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign` -> `sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> Celery `sync_assignee_outbound` via `assignment_source_dict`) and is not stored on the `GroupAssignee` model/row (no new field or persistence in `groupassignee.py`). Also, `sync_assignee_outbound` uses the task’s snapshotted `user_id`/`assign` to call `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(...)` and does not re-check the current DB assignee before syncing, so out-of-order execution of multiple queued tasks could apply a stale assignment externally. However, the finding references Celery retry settings and other behavior not visible in this diff, so whether this is a newly introduced defect vs. a pre-existing race can’t be fully verified from the patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411 — sync_status_outbound`'s new `assignment_source` parameter is dead: it has no callers anywhere in the codebase (unlike `sync_assignee_outbound`, there is no `sync_status_outbound` task/caller), and even if invoked, `should_sync("outbound_status", ...)` is never called with a source, so the cycle-prevention guard added to `should_sync` is only wired for assignee sync, not status sync, leaving inconsistent/incomplete abstraction across the two sync paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly wires `AssignmentSource` through the assignee outbound path (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` → task `sync_assignee_outbound` → `installation.should_sync(..., parsed_assignment_source)` and `sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`). In contrast, `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound` is updated to accept `assignment_source` (issues.py) but this diff shows no corresponding propagation of a source into any status-sync caller, nor any `should_sync("outbound_status", sync_source=...)` usage. That makes the abstraction inconsistent/incomplete within the scope of the changes. However, the claim that `sync_status_outbound` has “no callers anywhere in the codebase” cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 — queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition/import time, not per-instance, so every `AssignmentSource` created via `from_integration()` (the only production constructor path, used in src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:96-99 and :115-119) gets the same frozen "queued" timestamp for the life of the worker process, silently breaking any staleness/ordering check that relies on it.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`, the dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` at import/class-definition time, so all `AssignmentSource()` instances created without an explicit `queued` (including `from_integration()` which only passes `source_name` and `integration_id`) will share the same timestamp for the lifetime of the process. This is a real Python/dataclasses default-value pitfall; it should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to be per-instance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:17 — queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default evaluated once at class-definition/import time, not per-instance, so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` (i.e. every real call via `from_integration`) shares one stale timestamp; `test_to_dict` in tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py only asserts `queued is not None`, so this bug is not caught.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the dataclass field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`). That calls `timezone.now()` at import/class-definition time, so every instance created without an explicit `queued` (including `from_integration`, which does not pass `queued`) will share the same stale timestamp. The added test `test_to_dict` only checks that `queued` is present, not that it differs across instances, so it would not catch this.
